summary: Do not ship this design yet. The proposed gate remains fail-open for partial secret removal, and the claimed strict-scope contract does not actually enforce SealedSecrets scope.
triage: review-gate SKILL.md rules govern: render EVERY finding as a full table row, the human decides each row (accept/reject/defer/question — free text), echo back before applying, max 2 rounds, append decisions.md and COMMIT it with this artifact.

findings.title: The wiring gate validates only one direction of the state invariant
findings.body: The checks run only when the conventional sealed file exists. Removing that file and its kustomization entry while leaving the app-specific envFrom/checksum therefore passes the proposed gate. ArgoCD can then prune the SealedSecret and its generated Secret while existing pods retain stale environment values; later restarts fail. A dangling resource entry can instead break rendering. Both are partial states the claimed fail-closed gate misses.
findings.recommendation: Define an all-or-none invariant for the app-specific sealed file, non-optional envFrom reference, kustomization resource, and checksum. Reject partial states and unexpected app sealed filenames; test deletion and rename paths in both directions.

findings.title: Metadata equality does not enforce strict SealedSecrets scope
findings.body: The test matrix labels namespace equality as strict-scope, but kubeseal supports namespace-wide and cluster-wide scope through annotations. A manifest with the expected prod namespace and app name plus a cluster-wide annotation passes every listed validation, weakening name/namespace isolation and permitting ciphertext reuse outside the intended Secret. The wiring gate would not catch a manual scope-widening edit either.
findings.recommendation: Make scope part of the sealed contract: reject all namespace-wide/cluster-wide scope annotations, including supported compatibility spellings, in both readSealed and the repository gate. Add focused tests and classify this as an intentional policy tightening rather than behavior preservation.

next_steps: Revise the gate around a bidirectional sealed/secretless state model.
Add explicit strict-scope enforcement, then repeat the adversarial design review.
